_meta.description: Agent Brain Platform — Technique Registry seed data

techniques.name: RAG
techniques.description: Fetches relevant documents from a vector store at query time and injects them into the LLM context, grounding responses in retrieved knowledge.
techniques.theory_note: Reduces hallucination by anchoring generation to retrieved evidence; separates parametric (model weights) from non-parametric (retrieval) memory.
techniques.example_use_case: SAP Joule agent retrieves relevant ERP config docs before answering a business process question.
references: Lewis et al. 2020 — Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

techniques.name: API Polling
techniques.description: Periodically fetches live state from external APIs — REST, SOAP, GraphQL — to keep the agent's world model current.
techniques.theory_note: Simple but effective for event-driven perception where push-based streaming is unavailable.
techniques.example_use_case: Procurement agent polls SAP Ariba API every 30 seconds to track live bid status.

techniques.name: Document Parser
techniques.description: Extracts structured information from PDFs, tables, HTML, Word docs, and other document formats.
techniques.theory_note: Transforms unstructured documents into machine-readable facts the reasoning layer can operate on.
techniques.example_use_case: Contract review agent parses uploaded PDF contracts and extracts clause-level facts.

techniques.name: Sensor Fusion
techniques.description: Combines multiple heterogeneous sensor streams — camera, lidar, IMU, microphone — into a unified perceptual representation.
techniques.theory_note: Kalman filter and particle filter variants are standard; reduces uncertainty via multi-modal redundancy.
techniques.example_use_case: Warehouse robot fuses camera + lidar + proximity sensors to navigate safely.
references: Kalman 1960 — A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems

techniques.name: Web Scraper
techniques.description: Extracts live data from web pages via HTML parsing, headless browsers, or structured APIs.
techniques.example_use_case: Competitive intelligence agent monitors competitor pricing pages daily.

techniques.name: Markov State
techniques.description: Compresses raw observation history into a compact sufficient statistic such that future states are conditionally independent of the past given the present state.
techniques.theory_note: Satisfies the Markov Property: P(s_{t+1}|s_t) = P(s_{t+1}|s_t,s_{t-1},...). Required for MDP/Q-learning to be theoretically valid.
techniques.example_use_case: Chess engine compresses full board state into a 64-cell feature vector satisfying Markov Property.
references: Sutton & Barto 2018 — Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, Ch.3

techniques.name: RNN / LSTM
techniques.full_name: Recurrent Neural Network / Long Short-Term Memory
techniques.description: Learns a compressed recurrent hidden state from raw sequential observations, handling partial observability by remembering relevant history.
techniques.theory_note: LSTM gates prevent vanishing gradients; particularly effective in POMDPs where the state cannot be observed directly.
techniques.example_use_case: Trading agent encodes the last 60 price ticks into a hidden state for position-sizing decisions.
references: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber 1997 — Long Short-Term Memory

techniques.name: Belief State (Bayesian)
techniques.description: Maintains a probability distribution over all possible world states, updated via Bayes rule upon each new observation. The standard formulation for POMDPs.
techniques.theory_note: b'(s') = P(o|s',a) * sum_{s} P(s'|s,a)*b(s) / P(o|a,b). Exact update is exponential; particle filters approximate it.
techniques.example_use_case: Search-and-rescue drone maintains belief over survivor locations given noisy sensor readings.
references: Kaelbling et al. 1998 — Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains

techniques.name: Attention Mechanism
techniques.description: Uses multi-head self-attention over input history tokens to selectively weight relevant observations, producing a contextual state representation.
techniques.theory_note: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V. Handles long sequences without vanishing gradients.
techniques.example_use_case: Document Q&A agent attends over a 10k-token context to answer questions about specific clauses.
references: Vaswani et al. 2017 — Attention Is All You Need

techniques.name: Vector DB
techniques.description: Stores embeddings of past interactions, documents, and facts. Retrieves the most semantically similar records via approximate nearest-neighbor search.
techniques.theory_note: Enables long-term declarative memory without token budget constraints. FAISS, Pinecone, Chroma are common implementations.
techniques.example_use_case: Customer service agent retrieves the 5 most similar past resolved tickets to inform its response.
references: Johnson et al. 2019 — Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs (FAISS)

techniques.name: Episodic Buffer
techniques.description: Stores complete interaction episodes (state-action-reward sequences) that can be replayed for offline learning or contextual reference.
techniques.theory_note: Experience replay (DQN) samples mini-batches from the episodic buffer to break temporal correlation during training.
techniques.example_use_case: Game-playing agent replays its last 1M steps to improve Q-network without re-running the game.
references: Mnih et al. 2015 — Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning (DQN)

techniques.name: Working Memory
techniques.description: Maintains a short-term scratchpad of current task state, intermediate results, and tool outputs within the LLM's active context window.
techniques.theory_note: Analogous to human working memory — limited capacity, fast access, used for multi-step reasoning chains.
techniques.example_use_case: Coding agent keeps track of the current file, error message, and attempted fixes in its scratchpad.

techniques.name: Knowledge Graph
techniques.description: Stores factual knowledge as a structured graph of entities and typed relations, enabling multi-hop reasoning and logical queries.
techniques.theory_note: Combines symbolic precision with traversal-based reasoning. SPARQL / Cypher enable structured retrieval.
techniques.example_use_case: SAP ERP agent navigates a knowledge graph of business objects (PO → Vendor → Contract → GR) to answer cross-entity queries.

techniques.name: LLM
techniques.description: Uses a large language model as the core reasoning engine — interprets state, integrates memory, generates decisions and plans in natural language.
techniques.theory_note: Emergent few-shot and zero-shot reasoning from scale. Strengths: language understanding, generalization. Weaknesses: hallucination, latency.
techniques.example_use_case: SAP order processing agent interprets a purchase order email and decides whether to auto-approve or escalate.
references: Brown et al. 2020 — Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

techniques.name: MDP Policy
techniques.description: A formal state-to-action mapping derived by solving the Bellman equations — either via value iteration, policy iteration, or Q-learning.
techniques.theory_note: Optimal policy pi*(s) = argmax_a Q*(s,a). Requires known or learned transition and reward models. Guarantees optimality under the Markov assumption.
techniques.example_use_case: Inventory reorder agent derives optimal order-quantity policy from learned demand transition model.
references: Bellman 1957 — A Markovian Decision Process
Sutton & Barto 2018 Ch.4

techniques.name: Chain-of-Thought
techniques.description: Prompts the LLM to reason step-by-step through a problem before producing the final answer, significantly improving accuracy on complex tasks.
techniques.theory_note: Empirically shown to improve arithmetic, symbolic, and commonsense reasoning in LLMs at sufficient scale (>100B params).
techniques.example_use_case: Contract compliance agent reasons step-by-step through each clause before issuing a risk rating.
references: Wei et al. 2022 — Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

techniques.name: Bayesian Inference
techniques.description: Reasons under uncertainty by maintaining and updating probability distributions over hypotheses using Bayes' theorem: P(H|D) ∝ P(D|H)P(H).
techniques.theory_note: Principled uncertainty quantification. Sample-efficient but computationally expensive for high-dimensional state spaces.
techniques.example_use_case: Fraud detection agent updates its probability estimate of fraud given each new transaction signal.
references: Ghahramani 2015 — Probabilistic machine learning and artificial intelligence

techniques.name: Rule Engine
techniques.description: Executes explicit if-then-else rules to produce decisions deterministically. No learning required — behavior is fully specified by the rule set.
techniques.theory_note: Zero uncertainty, fully auditable, zero training data needed. Brittle to edge cases not covered by rules.
techniques.example_use_case: Credit approval agent applies regulatory compliance rules (Tier-1 capital ratio, KYC status) before any ML scoring.

techniques.name: MCTS
techniques.description: Builds a search tree via stochastic simulation rollouts, balancing exploration of new branches (UCB) against exploitation of promising ones.
techniques.theory_note: Four phases per iteration: Selection (UCB), Expansion, Simulation (rollout), Backpropagation. Scales to large branching factors without full lookahead.
techniques.example_use_case: Bidding strategy agent simulates thousands of auction outcomes to determine optimal bid price.
references: Browne et al. 2012 — A Survey of Monte Carlo Tree Search Methods
Silver et al. 2016 — AlphaGo

techniques.name: Minimax
techniques.description: Searches an adversarial game tree assuming the opponent plays optimally — maximizes own score while minimizing the opponent's best response.
techniques.theory_note: Minimax theorem (Von Neumann): in zero-sum games, max(min(V)) = min(max(V)). Alpha-beta pruning reduces complexity from O(b^d) to O(b^{d/2}).
techniques.example_use_case: Vendor negotiation agent models the counterparty as a rational adversary and plans optimal counter-offers.
references: Von Neumann & Morgenstern 1944 — Theory of Games and Economic Behavior

techniques.name: MDP Planning
techniques.description: Computes an optimal policy over a known state-transition model using value iteration or policy iteration, solving the Bellman optimality equations.
techniques.theory_note: Value iteration: V_{k+1}(s) = max_a [R(s,a) + γ * sum_{s'} P(s'|s,a)*V_k(s')]. Converges to V* for finite MDPs.
techniques.example_use_case: Supply chain routing agent solves an MDP over warehouse-to-customer delivery states to minimize expected cost.
references: Sutton & Barto 2018 — Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, Ch.4

techniques.name: LLM Planner
techniques.description: Uses an LLM to decompose a high-level goal into an ordered sequence of sub-tasks in natural language, optionally with tool specifications.
techniques.theory_note: ReAct and HuggingGPT patterns. Flexible but non-optimal — quality depends on prompt engineering and model capability.
techniques.example_use_case: HR onboarding agent plans a multi-day new-hire checklist: create AD account → assign licenses → schedule orientation.
references: Yao et al. 2022 — ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

techniques.name: Hierarchical RL
techniques.description: Decomposes a long-horizon task into a hierarchy of sub-goals. A high-level policy selects sub-goals; low-level policies execute them.
techniques.theory_note: Options framework (Sutton et al.) formalizes sub-policies with initiation sets and termination conditions. Reduces temporal credit assignment problem.
techniques.example_use_case: Autonomous procurement agent decomposes 'source a component' into sub-goals: RFQ → evaluate bids → negotiate → PO.
references: Sutton et al. 1999 — Between MDPs and Semi-MDPs: A Framework for Temporal Abstraction in RL

techniques.name: A* Search
techniques.description: Finds the optimal path in a graph by combining actual path cost g(n) with an admissible heuristic estimate h(n) of remaining cost.
techniques.theory_note: Optimal and complete when h(n) is admissible (never overestimates). f(n) = g(n) + h(n). Standard in pathfinding and PDDL planners.
techniques.example_use_case: Logistics agent finds the optimal delivery route across a city graph given time-window constraints.
references: Hart et al. 1968 — A Formal Basis for the Heuristic Determination of Minimum Cost Paths

techniques.name: Value Function V(s)
techniques.description: Estimates the expected cumulative discounted reward from state s onwards under the current policy: V(s) = E[sum γ^t * r_t | s_0=s].
techniques.theory_note: Central to policy evaluation in RL. Bootstraps TD learning and drives policy improvement via the Bellman equations.
techniques.example_use_case: Portfolio management agent estimates the long-term value of holding each asset position.
references: Sutton & Barto 2018 — Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, Ch.3

techniques.name: Q-Function Q(s,a)
techniques.description: Estimates the expected cumulative reward of taking action a in state s: Q(s,a) = E[sum γ^t * r_t | s_0=s, a_0=a].
techniques.theory_note: Q-learning (Watkins 1989) learns Q* off-policy via TD updates. Deep Q-Networks (DQN) approximate it with a neural network.
techniques.example_use_case: Customer churn agent learns Q(customer_state, intervention) to pick the most valuable retention action.
references: Watkins 1989 — Learning from Delayed Rewards
Mnih et al. 2015 — DQN

techniques.name: Advantage A(s,a)
techniques.description: Measures how much better action a is relative to the average action from state s: A(s,a) = Q(s,a) - V(s).
techniques.theory_note: Reduces variance in policy gradient estimates. Central to Actor-Critic (A3C, A2C, PPO) algorithms.
techniques.example_use_case: Robot manipulation agent uses advantage to identify which specific joint movement improved the task outcome.
references: Mnih et al. 2016 — Asynchronous Methods for Deep RL (A3C)

techniques.name: RLHF Reward Model
techniques.description: A learned reward model trained from human pairwise preferences, replacing the hand-engineered reward signal with a model of human intent.
techniques.theory_note: Reward model r_θ(x,y) is trained on preference data; the policy is then fine-tuned via PPO to maximize r_θ. Enables aligning to subtle human values.
techniques.example_use_case: Content moderation agent trained on human moderator preference data to flag borderline content accurately.
references: Ouyang et al. 2022 — Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (InstructGPT)

techniques.name: Thompson Sampling
techniques.description: Samples an action by drawing from the posterior distribution of expected rewards, naturally balancing exploration and exploitation.
techniques.theory_note: Bayesian-optimal for the multi-armed bandit. Regret: O(sqrt(KT log K)) — matches information-theoretic lower bounds.
techniques.example_use_case: A/B test agent dynamically allocates traffic to the better-performing variant without pre-committing sample sizes.
references: Russo et al. 2018 — A Tutorial on Thompson Sampling

techniques.name: UCB
techniques.description: Selects actions with the highest upper confidence bound on expected reward: UCB = mean_reward + c * sqrt(ln(t) / n_pulls). Optimistic in the face of uncertainty.
techniques.theory_note: Achieves O(log T) regret — logarithmically optimal. UCB1 variant is parameter-free.
techniques.example_use_case: Ad placement agent uses UCB to balance showing proven high-CTR ads against testing new creatives.
references: Auer et al. 2002 — Finite-time Analysis of the Multiarmed Bandit Problem

techniques.name: ε-Greedy
techniques.description: Exploits the best-known action with probability 1-ε and explores uniformly at random with probability ε.
techniques.theory_note: Simplest exploration strategy. Works but is inefficient — uniform random exploration is wasteful. Decaying ε-schedule improves convergence.
techniques.example_use_case: Recommendation system explores new content with 5% probability, exploits known-good picks otherwise.
references: Sutton & Barto 2018 — Ch.2 Multi-Armed Bandits

techniques.name: Curiosity-Driven Exploration
techniques.description: Generates an intrinsic reward signal proportional to prediction error on a forward model — the agent is rewarded for visiting surprising states.
techniques.theory_note: ICM: r_i = ||f(s_t, a_t) - s_{t+1}||^2. Allows exploration in sparse-reward environments without extrinsic signal.
techniques.example_use_case: Robot exploration agent maps an unknown factory floor using curiosity-driven path selection.
references: Pathak et al. 2017 — Curiosity-driven Exploration by Self-Supervised Prediction

techniques.name: Boltzmann / Softmax
techniques.description: Selects actions proportionally to exponentiated Q-values: P(a|s) = exp(Q(s,a)/τ) / sum_b exp(Q(s,b)/τ), where τ is temperature.
techniques.theory_note: Temperature τ → 0 is greedy; τ → ∞ is uniform. Gradient-based temperature annealing possible.
techniques.example_use_case: Dialogue agent softmax-samples response styles, producing varied conversation while preferring higher-scored options.

techniques.name: Tool Use
techniques.description: Invokes external tools — functions, APIs, MCP servers — via structured function calls parsed from LLM output.
techniques.theory_note: Standard mechanism for grounding LLM agents in real-world effects. Anthropic MCP standardizes tool schemas.
techniques.example_use_case: SAP Joule agent calls BAPI_PO_CREATE to create a purchase order after reasoning through the approval chain.
references: Anthropic MCP Spec 2024

techniques.name: API Call
techniques.description: Executes direct HTTP/REST/SOAP/GraphQL calls to external systems with structured payloads.
techniques.example_use_case: ERP agent calls SAP S/4HANA OData API to update inventory levels after goods receipt.

techniques.name: Code Execution
techniques.description: Generates and executes code in a sandboxed environment, allowing the agent to perform arbitrary computation as an action.
techniques.example_use_case: Data analysis agent writes and runs Python to aggregate a CSV before summarizing results.

techniques.name: RPA
techniques.description: Automates UI-level interactions with legacy systems that lack APIs — mouse clicks, form fills, screen reading.
techniques.example_use_case: Finance agent uses RPA to extract monthly report data from a legacy SAP GUI transaction (SE16).

techniques.name: Physical Actuator
techniques.description: Sends control signals to physical hardware — motors, grippers, valves, industrial controllers.
techniques.example_use_case: Warehouse pick-and-place robot sends joint angles to arm controller after vision-based object localization.

techniques.name: Reward Signal
techniques.description: A scalar R_t returned from the environment after each action, serving as the primary training signal for the RL agent.
techniques.theory_note: Reward hypothesis: all goals and purposes of an agent can be framed as maximization of cumulative reward. R_t must be designed to avoid reward hacking.
techniques.example_use_case: Customer satisfaction score at end of service interaction used as reward to train the service agent.
references: Sutton & Barto 2018 — Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, Ch.1

techniques.name: TD Learning
techniques.description: Updates value estimates incrementally after each step using the TD error: δ_t = r_t + γ*V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t). Bootstraps from incomplete episodes.
techniques.theory_note: Unifies Monte Carlo (full episode) and dynamic programming (known model) approaches. TD(0), TD(λ), and Q-learning are all TD methods.
techniques.example_use_case: Stock trading agent updates its value estimates after each trade without waiting for the full portfolio evaluation cycle.
references: Sutton 1988 — Learning to Predict by the Methods of Temporal Differences

techniques.name: Policy Gradient
techniques.description: Directly optimizes the policy parameters by ascending the gradient of expected return: ∇J(θ) = E[∇log π_θ(a|s) * Q(s,a)].
techniques.theory_note: REINFORCE (Williams 1992) is high variance; Actor-Critic and PPO reduce variance with baseline subtraction. Standard for continuous action spaces.
techniques.example_use_case: Dialog agent fine-tuned with PPO using human preference reward model to improve response quality.
references: Schulman et al. 2017 — Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms

techniques.name: RLHF
techniques.description: Collects human pairwise preference ratings on outputs, trains a reward model, then fine-tunes the policy via PPO to align with human values.
techniques.theory_note: Three-phase: supervised fine-tuning → reward model training on human preferences → PPO optimization of policy against reward model.
techniques.example_use_case: Customer-facing LLM agent aligned to enterprise tone-of-voice guidelines via RLHF on agent-reviewer ratings.
references: Ouyang et al. 2022 — InstructGPT
Christiano et al. 2017 — Deep RL from Human Preferences

techniques.name: Critic Update
techniques.description: Updates the critic (value) network from rollout data so it more accurately estimates V(s) or Q(s,a), providing a lower-variance baseline for the actor.
techniques.theory_note: Alternates actor (policy) and critic (value) gradient updates. A3C, A2C, SAC, TD3 all implement actor-critic loops.
techniques.example_use_case: Multi-robot coordination system maintains separate critic per agent, sharing value estimates for cooperative task.
references: Mnih et al. 2016 — Asynchronous Methods for Deep RL (A3C)

techniques.name: Constitutional AI
techniques.description: Uses a set of principle rules (a 'constitution') to guide the agent in critiquing and revising its own outputs — self-critique loop for alignment.
techniques.theory_note: Developed by Anthropic: RLHF from AI feedback (RLAIF) where the AI itself rates outputs against constitutional principles, reducing human labeling burden.
techniques.example_use_case: Enterprise AI assistant applies a constitution of data privacy and compliance rules before each user-facing response.
references: Bai et al. 2022 — Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

techniques.name: Reward Shaping
techniques.description: Adds auxiliary reward terms that guide the agent away from unsafe states or toward safe behaviors, without changing the optimal policy.
techniques.theory_note: Potential-based reward shaping F(s,a,s') = γΦ(s') - Φ(s) preserves the optimal policy while accelerating convergence and steering behavior.
techniques.example_use_case: Surgical robot's RL policy receives negative reward shaping for proximity to critical anatomy structures.
references: Ng et al. 1999 — Policy Invariance Under Reward Transformations

techniques.name: Policy Constraints
techniques.description: Applies hard constraints on the agent's action space — certain actions are categorically prohibited regardless of the policy's preference.
techniques.theory_note: Constrained MDP (CMDP) formalism: maximize expected reward subject to constraint E[sum C_t] <= d. Lagrangian relaxation converts to unconstrained problem.
techniques.example_use_case: Finance agent is hard-constrained from initiating any transaction above €1M without dual approval.
references: Altman 1999 — Constrained Markov Decision Processes

techniques.name: Output Filtering
techniques.description: Classifies and blocks unsafe, off-policy, or non-compliant agent outputs before they are executed or shown to users.
techniques.theory_note: Defense-in-depth layer. Does not improve the policy but catches edge cases and provides a hard safety net at execution time.
techniques.example_use_case: HR chatbot output filtered to prevent disclosure of salary ranges or legal advice before user response.

techniques.name: Single-Agent Loop
techniques.description: Classic perceive → encode → reason → plan → act → observe loop for a single autonomous agent.
techniques.theory_note: The agent loop is the foundational execution pattern. All other orchestration patterns extend or compose it.
techniques.example_use_case: Simple approval routing agent: perceive email → classify request → decide approve/reject → send response.

techniques.name: Multi-Agent Coordination
techniques.description: Coordinates multiple specialized agents that communicate, share observations, and divide task responsibility.
techniques.theory_note: Cooperative: maximize joint reward. Competitive: Nash equilibrium strategies. Communication protocols (MARL, DIAL) enable emergent coordination.
techniques.example_use_case: Procurement suite: Sourcing Agent, Negotiation Agent, and Compliance Agent coordinate via shared message bus.
references: Lowe et al. 2017 — Multi-Agent Actor-Critic for Mixed Cooperative-Competitive Environments

techniques.name: Hierarchical Orchestration
techniques.description: A manager agent decomposes a complex task into sub-tasks and dispatches them to specialized worker agents, collecting and integrating results.
techniques.theory_note: Mirrors hierarchical RL in the cognitive layer. Manager operates on abstract sub-goal space; workers on concrete action space.
techniques.example_use_case: Order-to-Cash orchestration: Manager agent routes sub-tasks to Credit Check Agent, Fulfillment Agent, and Invoice Agent.

techniques.name: ReAct Loop
techniques.description: Interleaves LLM reasoning traces with tool-use actions — the agent alternates between Thought, Action, and Observation steps.
techniques.theory_note: ReAct (Yao et al. 2022) outperforms pure chain-of-thought and pure action approaches on knowledge-intensive tasks by grounding reasoning in observations.
techniques.example_use_case: Research agent alternates between reasoning about what to look up and calling search/retrieval tools to gather evidence.
references: Yao et al. 2022 — ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
